feature: Custom hooks: batch length assertion over RabbitMQ
goalOneSentence: Write custom Generator/Assertion/Probe hooks plus runner YAML so a RabbitMQ round-trip of 10 JSON-array batches is verified hermetic and every batch has exactly 5 items.

tasks.title: Scaffold the Telemetry hook-runner project
tasks.description: Create folder Telemetry/ containing Telemetry.csproj and Program.cs for a QaaS runner that will host CUSTOM HOOKS. csproj: Project Sdk=Microsoft.NET.Sdk; PropertyGroup with OutputType Exe, TargetFramework net10.0, ImplicitUsings enable, Nullable enable; PackageReference QaaS.Runner Version="*" AND QaaS.Common.Assertions Version="*" (needed for HermeticByInputOutputPercentage); ItemGroup with None Update="telemetry.qaas.yaml" CopyToOutputDirectory Always (the yaml is created by a later task; the csproj entry must exist now). Program.cs must be exactly one statement: QaaS.Runner.Bootstrap.New(args).Run(); Hooks compiled INSIDE the runner project assembly are discovered automatically — no extra wiring or registration code is needed, do NOT add any. Do not create the yaml or any .cs hook files in this task. Build must succeed even though the yaml does not exist yet.
acceptanceCriteria: Program.cs is the one-line Bootstrap call
Both QaaS.Runner and QaaS.Common.Assertions referenced with Version="*"
rubric: csproj matches the verified runner shape exactly
failureModes: Adding Main method boilerplate around Bootstrap (not needed with top-level statement)
Forgetting QaaS.Common.Assertions so HermeticByInputOutputPercentage cannot resolve

tasks.title: Author the three custom hooks (Generator, Assertion, Probe)
tasks.description: In the existing Telemetry/ project (csproj already references QaaS.Runner Version="*"; the QaaS.Framework.SDK namespaces come transitively from it — add NO new package references), write three hook classes in namespace Telemetry. (1) JsonArrayGenerator.cs: record JsonArrayGeneratorConfiguration { [Required] public uint? Count { get; set; } and public uint NumberOfItemsPerArray { get; set; } = 5; } (using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations). Class JsonArrayGenerator : BaseGenerator<JsonArrayGeneratorConfiguration> (usings: System.Collections.Immutable, System.Text.Json.Nodes, QaaS.Framework.SDK.DataSourceObjects, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Hooks.Generator, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Session.DataObjects, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Session.SessionDataObjects) overriding public override IEnumerable<Data<object>> Generate(IImmutableList<SessionData> sessionDataList, IImmutableList<DataSource> dataSourceList): loop Configuration.Count times, build a System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonArray with Configuration.NumberOfItemsPerArray items (e.g. jsonArray.Add("SomeItem")), and yield return new Data<object> { Body = jsonArray };. (2) LengthAssertion.cs: record LengthAssertionConfiguration { [Required] public uint? ExpectedLength { get; set; } [Required] public string? OutputName { get; set; } }. Class LengthAssertion : BaseAssertion<LengthAssertionConfiguration> (usings: System.Collections.Immutable, System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations, System.Text.Json.Nodes, QaaS.Framework.Serialization, QaaS.Framework.SDK.DataSourceObjects, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Extensions, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Hooks.Assertion, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Session.SessionDataObjects) overriding public override bool Assert(IImmutableList<SessionData> sessionDataList, IImmutableList<DataSource> dataSourceList): var output = sessionDataList.AsSingle().GetOutputByName(Configuration.OutputName!).CastCommunicationData<JsonArray>(); collect entries of output.Data whose item.Body?.Count != Configuration.ExpectedLength (track index and actual length); set AssertionMessage to a count summary; set AssertionTrace to per-index detail lines (or an all-good sentence); AssertionAttachments.Add(new AssertionAttachment { Path = "length-assertion/summary.json", Data = <anonymous summary object>, SerializationType = SerializationType.Json }); return true only when no mismatches. (3) PrintCurrentTimeProbe.cs: class PrintCurrentTimeProbe : BaseProbe<object> (usings: System.Collections.Immutable, QaaS.Framework.SDK.DataSourceObjects, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Hooks.Probe, QaaS.Framework.SDK.Session.SessionDataObjects) overriding public override void Run(IImmutableList<SessionData> sessionDataList, IImmutableList<DataSource> dataSourceList) { Console.WriteLine($"Current time is: {DateTime.UtcNow}"); }. NOTE the exact shapes: generator yields Data<object> (NOT DataSource), probe is BaseProbe<object> with Run(...) (NOT a parameterless Probe()). Build must stay green.
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build succeeds with the three hook files
Configuration records use nullable properties with [Required]
Assertion sets AssertionMessage, AssertionTrace and adds an attachment
rubric: Hook base classes and namespaces exactly match the SDK (no invented interfaces like IAssertion)
Generator yields DataSource objects with CommunicationData<JsonArray> payloads
failureModes: Returning bool without setting AssertionMessage/AssertionTrace (useless diagnostics)

tasks.title: Author telemetry.qaas.yaml and prove the pipeline green end-to-end
tasks.description: Create Telemetry/telemetry.qaas.yaml wiring the custom hooks by CLASS NAME. MetaData: Team: Smoke, System: Telemetry. DataSources: one entry Name: 10Batches, Generator: JsonArrayGenerator, GeneratorConfiguration: { Count: 10, NumberOfItemsPerArray: 5 }. Sessions: one session Name: TelemetryRoundTrip with Probes: [- Probe: PrintCurrentTimeProbe, Name: GetCurrentTime], Publishers: one Name: Publisher, DataSourceNames: [10Batches] (PLURAL key, list value — FB s13#3), Policies: [- LoadBalance: { Rate: 50 }], RabbitMq: { Host: 127.0.0.1, Username: admin, Password: admin, RoutingKey: /, Port: 5672, ExchangeName: c02-input }, Serialize: { Serializer: Json }; Consumers: one Name: Consumer, TimeoutMs: 5000, RabbitMq: { Host: 127.0.0.1, Username: admin, Password: admin, RoutingKey: /, Port: 5672, ExchangeName: c02-output }, Deserialize: { Deserializer: Json }. Assertions: (1) Name+Assertion HermeticByInputOutputPercentage, SessionNames: [TelemetryRoundTrip], AssertionConfiguration: { OutputNames: [Consumer], InputNames: [Publisher], ExpectedPercentage: 100 }; (2) Name+Assertion LengthAssertion, SessionNames: [TelemetryRoundTrip], AssertionConfiguration: { OutputName: Consumer, ExpectedLength: 5 }. A RabbitMQ broker runs on 127.0.0.1:5672 (admin/admin) and the verify step itself starts a relay that moves messages from exchange c02-input to c02-output, so the run must end exit 0 with both assertions passing.
acceptanceCriteria: template validation exits 0 with no 'not found in' warnings
e2e run with relay exits 0 (hermetic 100%, all batches length 5)

verify.cmd: $r = Start-Process powershell -ArgumentList '-NoProfile','-ExecutionPolicy','Bypass','-File','..\relay.ps1','-InputExchange','c02-input','-OutputExchange','c02-output','-TimeoutSec','150' -PassThru; Start-Sleep -Seconds 10; dotnet run -c Release -- run telemetry.qaas.yaml; $code = $LASTEXITCODE; Stop-Process -Id $r.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit $code

rubric: Hook names in YAML match the C# class names exactly
Both assertions configured per their configuration records
No invented YAML keys (template gate stays silent)
failureModes: Wrong exchange names so consumer times out and hermetic drops below 100
TimeoutMs too low for relay latency (keep 5000)
